There are two ways to use those skills here:

---

## Option 1: Install as global Claude slash commands (simplest)
Clone the repo and put the `.md` files into `~/.claude/commands/`. Claude Code picks them up automatically as `/spec`, `/plan`, etc.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills /tmp/agent-skills
mkdir -p ~/.claude/commands
cp /tmp/agent-skills/skills/*.md ~/.claude/commands/
```

Then you (or the agent executor) can invoke them directly — e.g. `/build implement log
If i use option 3, it will replace my existing agents right?

No — agent-skills are **slash commands** (prompt templates), not code. They wouldn't touch or replace any of your existing files like `src/agents/CommunicationAgent.js`.

They work at the Claude Code session level: when invoked (e.g. `/build`), they inject a structured prompt into the conversation to guide the AI's approach. Your actual agent code remains unchanged.

The only thing any option would add is `.md` files — either in `~/.claude/commands/` (global) or a local `.claude/commands/` folde

I am still not following. Which part of my repo and workflow will these skills replace? How will it be better for my REA system?
Or you think it is not needed and my agents are already good enough

Your REA system already has dedicated agents (`PlanningAgent.js`, `ReviewAgent.js`, `PRAgent.js`, etc.) that **do what those skills do** — but as running Node.js code, not just prompt templates.

Here's the honest comparison:

| agent-skills | Your REA system |
|---|---|
| `/plan` — prompts Claude to make a plan | `PlanningAgent.js` — runs Claude, stores plan, hands off to next agent |
| `/review` — prompts Claude to review code | `ReviewAgent.js` — runs Claude review as part of automated pipeli
Wow happy to know my system is already superior to those skills

Your REA system is genuinely well-architected — it takes what those skills do as one-shot prompts and turns them into an automated, stateful pipeline with handoffs, memory, and WhatsApp delivery. That's a significant step up.
